title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts (+ OpenAI compatibility)
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Streaming connections in the field were not robust to client-side cancellations, abrupt disconnects, or transient network flaps. This resulted in leaked server-side stream state and KV cache entries, duplicate completions on reconnect, and occasional user-facing timeouts. We need deterministic lifecycle controls that harmonize server-side timeouts, client cancel semantics, and reconnect/resume behavior while preserving OpenAI compatibility for streaming clients.

What this change does: 1) Introduces a ConnectionManager that centralizes lifecycle state (connected, draining, cancelled, resumed). 2) Adds a reconnect/resume protocol handshake that reconciles in-progress generation cursor and token-accumulated checksum. 3) Implements explicit server-side idle/lease timeouts with graceful draining and force-terminate paths to prevent resource leaks. 4) Adds a client-cancel path that immediately marks streams as cancelled and triggers configurable KV-cache rollback where applicable. 5) Adds an OpenAI-compat adapter that maps existing OpenAI streaming semantics to the new lifecycle, including support for compatibility headers and the close_with_reason event.

Files touched (high level): service/streaming/connection_manager.py - new lifecycle controller; service/streaming/protocol.py - reconnect/resume handshake and wire-level changes; runtime/inference/kv_cache.py - safe eviction hooks; openai_compat/streams_adapter.go - compatibility glue for external clients; sdk/ts/streaming.ts - client-side reconnect helpers (backoff/resume token); docs/streaming.md - operational guidance and rollout notes; tests/streaming/* - new unit and integration tests.

Design notes: - Reconnect/resume uses a lightweight resume token (generation_id + cursor + checksum) sent by client; server validates and replays remaining delta. If validation fails, server falls back to fresh generation after informing client. - Server idle lease default is 60s for hosted mode (configurable per-deployment). When lease expires server enters DRAINING: sends close_with_reason and frees long-lived resources after max_drain (5s) or immediate on force. - Client cancel sends a single Cancel frame; server acknowledges with cancelled status and triggers early KV cache eviction to avoid stale prefix reuse. - OpenAI compatibility: the adapter synthesizes the alt-close events and maps Redwood lifecycle codes to OpenAI stream close events so most existing clients need no change.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests: reconnection handshake, cancel ack, lease expiry -> drain path. - Integration: e2e streaming test against openai_compat adapter with simulated flaps. - Load test: no regression in throughput under steady-state; 2-4% p99 latency increase on worst-case reconnect storms (mitigated via exponential backoff config).

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging with openai_compat toggled off by default. 2) Canary in us-west with adapter on for synthetic consumers. 3) Gradual ramp to 20% by weight, monitoring stream errors, leaked connections, and token duplication counts. 4) Full rollout after 72h stable metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] ConnectionManager implementation
- [x] Reconnect/resume handshake and validation
- [x] Server lease and drain behavior
- [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping and headers
- [x] SDK helper functions for resume/backoff
- [x] Tests (unit/integration/load)
- [x] Docs and runbook updates

Notes: This is non-breaking for most hosted clients. Some bespoke clients that relied on infinite server-side state retention may need to set lease to a larger value. See docs/streaming.md for migration guidance.
